summary: Ten GitHub issues addressed in two isolated work groups: stable usernames across enrollment and account changes, and shared academic records with an explicit reference school year. A third branch combines both groups for integration verification.

followup.title: Program Profile Policy Follow-up
followup.summary: Adds a configurable Latin-name and offered-grade policy, simplifies Users & Roles, and makes the current program year authoritative in shared academic editors.

groups.title: Identity and Stable Usernames
changes: Preserve established account handles during setup, invitation redemption and enabling tutor participation; synchronize linked roster handles.
Reserve the namespace across User and Tutor records through transaction locks and a persistent guard; reject stale Serializable snapshots and retry only safe pre-dispatch approval failures.
Normalize accents, preserve full single-token names, offer an optional Latin spelling for non-Latin names, and fall back to member. Limit final handles to 64 characters, including collision suffixes.
Allocate verified student handles once and provide an explicit Head-only backfill for selected existing verified students.

groups.title: Shared Academic Profiles
changes: Record self-reported G1–G12 with a reference school year and confirmation history; preserve unknown and nonstandard reports.
Derive expected graduation from that reference year. Stop automatic grade advancement and require reconfirmation when known grades become stale.
Share canonical academic values across tutee, tutor, crew and mixed accounts, with version-protected self-service and authorized staff corrections.
Show grade, school year and expected graduation together in Users & Roles and account profiles. Preserve historical intake answers and stable usernames.

validation.title: Complete Automated Suite
items: npm test -- --maxWorkers=1: 1,570 tests passed across all 183 test files. Final run completed in 193 seconds.

Coverage includes real PostgreSQL cross-table username races, Serializable snapshot conflicts, bounded approval retries, account linking, verified intake, re-enrollment, migration preservation, academic transitions, permissions, stale edits and localized UI rendering.
Two integration mismatches found during the first full run were corrected: the registration response expectation and the Chinese peer-role glossary. The complete suite was rerun and passed.

items: npm run check: passed Next route type generation, ESLint and TypeScript. The 18 pre-existing lint warnings remain; there are no lint errors.
npm run docs:check: all 13 documentation tests passed.
npm run build: optimized Next.js 16.3.3 Turbopack production build passed using one build worker.
Evidence: final-check.log, final-docs.log and final-build.log in the review worktree .validation folder.

validation.title: Database Upgrade and Actual Browser Workflows
items: Applied both new migrations to an isolated database populated using the upstream schema and synthetic seed. Legacy crew grade 10 was preserved as unconfirmed, without inventing a reference year. Existing student usernames were not silently backfilled.
Self-service confirmation: Emma reported G10 for 26–27; expected graduation became 2029 and the staff view matched. Existing @emma remained unchanged.
Verified invitation registration: 李明 with optional Latin spelling Li Ming, G10 and reference year 26–27 completed with username lming29.
Explicit Head backfill: Kate Park moved from no assigned username to @kpark through the management UI.

Verified self-service and staff profile surfaces in English and Chinese at 1440-pixel desktop and 390-pixel phone widths. Checked wrapping, page overflow and mobile controls; new controls measured at least 44 pixels.
Captured 25 application images; the report embeds 20 selected screenshots. The portable HTML opens offline, its image preview works, and its mobile layout has no page overflow.
Machine-readable evidence: browser-evidence.json, identity-browser-evidence.json, migration-evidence.json and report-verification.json beside this report.

resources: Temporary web and PostgreSQL servers were stopped; ports 3100, 55439 and 55440 were verified closed. Browser contexts were closed after each run. Verification used synthetic local data, serial tests and one build worker. Automatic approval review rejected deletion of the generated .next and test caches with “blocked by policy”; these caches remain on disk. Source worktrees, logs, screenshots, task-local dependencies and demonstration databases are retained for review.

Reference-year confirmation is the agreed academic policy. Existing handles remain stable; optional Latin spelling is offered for new non-Latin names, with member as the fallback.
